chapter: Hightower: New Orleans parades and early players
title: Bunk Johnson's disappearance and Esquire concert
summary: He tells of Bunk's sudden rise, his leaving for a rice farm, and the later concert and New York trip.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Buddy Bolden and Buddy Petit: the trumpet legends

blocks.x: Yeah. They wanted me and I wouldn't even go. Because they had set up. Now they went down there and bought Bunk I think a set of teeth. And wait until he trained himself to them, see.
They bought him a suit of clothes. How did Bunk play when he was young?

Young? Yeah. He was, what the time that he was, he flew right straight on up there. He was just great. Just great. But as suddenly as it looked like it just was a flash, it just looked like he come up and played all of a sudden and everybody in the Orleans just went crazy. Then after a while we ain't got no Bunk. It was a funny thing. And he never come back no more.
He never come back. But this time they tell me they took him to New York. When was that? It was about five?
Oh, in 1945. I was there in New York when he was there.

Yeah, yeah. Well they tell me he was all right. Well, what he wanted to do, he was kind of fanatic. He was very thin. At the time that he was coming up and he was kind of flighty like, see. He wanted certain musicians I guess that he'd come in with so it seemed like after that concert was that he got an agent. I don't know who booked him in New York but they got Bechet for him and they formed a band
